questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

**A) **Each month in the modern Gregorian calendar consists of at least 28 days.

**B) **To fully sync the calendar with the lunar year, the Roman king Numa Pompilius added January and February to the original 10 months.

**C) **That number would be a nicely rounded 30 were it not for February.

**D)** It was altered after Numa’s addition including the shortening of February at certain intervals, and the addition of a leap day. February’s 28-day length has stuck.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**ACBD**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement A **is the opening sentence as it starts with a** general fact**. Each month in the modern Gregorian calendar consists of at least 28 days.
 
• **Statement C** is the next sentence as it mentions that **February is the only exception** to the fact given in the previous sentence.
 
• **Statement B **is the next sentence as it mentions that in the past **Roman ruler added two months**, January and February to the original 10 months.
 
• **Statement D **is the final sentence while ruler Numa made some additions **some changes were retained like that of the modern leap day**. This explains the **exception of February consisting of 28** days mentioned in the second statement.

Hence, the correct sequence is **ACBD.**

**The correct passage is: *A) ****Each month in the modern Gregorian calendar consists of at least 28 days. **C) **That number would be a nicely rounded 30 were it not for February. **B) **To fully sync the calendar with the lunar year, the Roman king Numa Pompilius added January and February to the original 10 months. **D)** It was altered after Numa’s addition including the shortening of February at certain intervals, and the addition of a leap day. February’s 28-day length has stuck.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

**A) **The phrasing was retained even after pants were made into one complete garment.

**B) **Calling them a pair of pants, as they were eventually known, made sense when there were two components.

**C) **They were put on one at a time and then secured around the waist.

**D) **According to some, the phrase “pair of pants” harkens back to the days when what constituted pants meant separate items, one for each leg.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DCBA**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement D **is the first sentence of the passage as it mentions the phrase "**pair of pants**" harkens back to the days when what constituted pants meant separate items, **one for each leg**. The theme of the passage is the phrase "**pair of pants**".
 
• **Statement C **is the second sentence of the passage as it mentions that in the past **pants were put on one at a time** and then secured around the **waist**. This explains the phrase "pair of pants" in the opening sentence.
 
• **Statement B **is the third sentence of the passage as it mentions that in the past the phrase made sense as pants were worn in that way. They were two components one for each leg like a pair of shoes.
 
• **Statement A **is the final sentence of the passage as it mentions that the **phrasing was retained even after they were made into one complete garment**.

Hence, the correct sequence is **DCBA**.

**The correct passage is: *D) ****According to some, the phrase “pair of pants” harkens back to the days when what constituted pants meant separate items, one for each leg. **C) **They were put on one at a time and then secured around the waist. **B) **Calling them a pair of pants, as they were eventually known, made sense when there were two components. **A) **The phrasing was retained even after pants were made into one complete garment.*

**Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. This cooled off into the darkness after a few million years.

B. The first time was when the universe began its existence as a glowing fireball.

C. In the modern scientific story, the light was created not once but twice.

D. The second time was when the cold material condensed into dense nuggets and ignited to become the first stars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CBAD.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'C' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "the creation of the light". Hence, 'C' is the first part.
 
• Sentence B will come after C as it is giving information about the first time creation of the light (when the universe began its existence as a glowing fireball).
 
• Sentence A will come after B as it is giving the reason (this cooled off into the darkness after a few million years) behind the need for the creation of the light for the second time.
 
• The sentence 'D' is the concluding part as it is giving information about the second time creation of the light (when the cold material is condensed into dense nuggets and ignited to become the first stars​).

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *In the modern scientific story, the light was created not once but twice. The first time was when the universe began its existence as a glowing fireball. This cooled off into the darkness after a few million years. The second time was when the cold material condensed into dense nuggets and ignited to become the first stars.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 __
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

** A) **Although we all obviously have different personalities and talents, there’s no reason to believe these differences can be explained by the dominance of one half of the brain over the other half.

** B) **One of the myth’s fatal flaws is that it relies on vague conceptions of the abilities it purports to explain.

** C) ** Recent research using brain imaging technology hasn’t found any evidence of right or left dominance.

** D) **The idea that there are right-brained and left-brained people is a myth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**DACB**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement D **is the opening sentence of the passage as it begins by mentioning **a myth**. The myth is that there are right-brained and left-brained people.
 
• **Statement A **is the second sentence of the passage as it begins with the **conjunction **"**although**". We use "although" as a **contrasting **idea in the main sentence to the second clause.
 
• **Statement C** is the third sentence of the passage as it **debunks the myth** by stating that recent research using brain imaging technology hasn’t found any evidence of right or left dominance.
 
• **Statement B** is the final sentence of the passage as it is a conclusion based on the previous sentences. We can see the logical flow of the sentences to arrive at a conclusion from the **myth **to the **truth**.

​Hence, the correct sequence is "**DACB**".

**The complete passage is**: D) The idea that there are right-brained and left-brained people is a myth. A) Although we all obviously have different personalities and talents, there’s no reason to believe these differences can be explained by the dominance of one half of the brain over the other half. C) Recent research using brain imaging technology hasn’t found any evidence of right or left dominance. B) One of the myth’s fatal flaws is that it relies on vague conceptions of the abilities it purports to explain.
